behavior: No LIVE WIRING for Ollama survives in tracked files. Checks the identifiers that would make it reachable - hostname, SSOT key path, middleware name, image, port - NOT the bare word. A word check cannot pass: 'videollamada' in the Calendly URL contains the substring, and every legitimate remaining mention is either the ace2 teardown (which needs the name) or a comment explaining why a catalog is now empty
evidence: 2026-08-09: exit 1 (no matches). Survivors are deliberate and named in the exclusions: the dev_node teardown removes /opt/ollama and port 11434 so it must keep the name; beelink_services keeps its idempotent cleanup per resolved Risk 3. The original word-based command was unsatisfiable and was rewritten - see behavior.

behavior: The drift gate is green and no generated artifact still carries an Ollama reference
evidence: 2026-08-09: `make validate-sync` -> 'All generated files in sync' (homepage, images, oidc). Generated artifacts carry no Ollama wiring. Note the first pass missed four homepage references - topology tables and the DNS diagram - which only surfaced because the generated custom.js still carried them after the source edit.

behavior: The prod API key is unset in SOPS, not merely de-registered from SECRET_CATALOG into an orphan no audit can see
verification: ! (poetry run toolkit secrets audit --env prod | grep -qi ollama) && ! (sops -d infra/config/secrets/prod.enc.yaml | grep -qi ollama)
evidence: 2026-08-09: `toolkit secrets unset apps.services.ai.ollama.api_key --env prod` removed the value, but left an empty `ollama: {}` node, and `ai` had no other child - so `apps.services.ai` was unset too. `sops -d prod.enc.yaml | grep -i ollama` now returns nothing. Unset BEFORE dropping the SECRET_CATALOG entry, which is the order that avoids leaving a value no audit can see.

behavior: The public Cloudflare record is destroyed and the name no longer resolves
evidence: 2026-08-09: `make tf-dns-plan` reported `Plan: 0 to add, 0 to change, 1 to destroy`, the single resource being cloudflare_record.kubelab_svc["ollama"] (A, ollama.kubelab.live -> 162.55.57.175, proxied=false, id b5a3dc58a24db92a83c1ed81c0f00c73). Terraform's stated reason is `because key ["ollama"] is not in for_each map` — the record was removed by shrinking the desired set in services.json (#915), which is why merging that PR was inert until the apply. Applied: outputs went kubelab_record_count 16 -> 15 and the ollama entry left kubelab_service_urls. Verified after: `dig +short ollama.kubelab.live @1.1.1.1` empty, and empty at the authoritative NS too, while api.kubelab.live still resolves (104.21.56.20 / 172.67.175.250) — so the zone was not damaged.

behavior: The out-of-band Middleware is gone from the LIVE prod cluster - the object Argo never tracked, so a git-only check cannot see it. NOTE: there is no backing Secret and there never was; the API key is inline in the Middleware spec (keys: [${API_KEY}] in api-key.yaml.tpl). The secret clause below is kept as a guard against a future variant, not because one existed
verification: ! kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/kubelab-prod-config get middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab 2>/dev/null && ! kubectl --kubeconfig ~/.kube/kubelab-prod-config get secret -n kubelab -o name 2>/dev/null | grep -qi ollama
evidence: 2026-08-09: before deletion `kubectl get middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab` returned it at AGE 78d, and `get secret -n kubelab -o name | grep -i ollama` was already empty — confirming no Secret ever backed it. Deleted with a supervised one-off (`kubectl delete middleware api-key-ollama -n kubelab`, authorized by Manu) because the toolkit has an apply path and no delete path; filed as its own gap. Post-check: both clauses pass. The two remaining ollama middlewares, ollama-inflight and ollama-ratelimit, are git-tracked in overlays/prod/ollama-throttle.yaml and are Argo's to prune on PR-B merge, not this probe's concern. Edge smoke after deletion: api.kubelab.live 200, auth.kubelab.live 200 — removing a middleware referenced by a soon-to-be-pruned IngressRoute did not affect other routers. Deleting it also removed a plaintext prod API key from etcd, since the key is inline in the Middleware spec rather than in a Secret.

behavior: The suites pass with the Ollama e2e module gone and no dangling expectation. Checks live wiring rather than the word: the remaining mentions in tests/ are comments recording what was removed and why, including the fixture shape worth copying for the next API-keyed service
verification: make test && ! (git grep -inE 'ollama\\.kubelab\\.live|apps\\.services\\.ai\\.ollama|api-key-ollama|ollama/ollama|:11434' -- tests/ | grep -vE ':[0-9]+: *#' | grep -q .)
evidence: 2026-08-09: `make test` -> 393 passed, 98 deselected (394 before; net -1 from replacing two ollama-coupled catalog tests with one generic invariant). tests/e2e/test_ollama_public.py deleted, expectations.py entry removed, the ollama_api_key fixture removed from conftest.py. The middleware tests were coupled to a business fact - that ollama was registered - so emptying the catalog broke all seven at once; they now drive the machinery from a synthetic spec.
